_doc: Hand decisions for tools/state_towns.py (re-run it after editing; never hand-edit towns.tsv). Sources: Census Gazetteer 2023 places, popest 2023 (incorporated), Gazetteer 2010 POP10 (CDPs).
_regions: First match wins. rio = the Rio Grande corridor (Espanola valley box, then Cochiti to San Antonio incl. the Albuquerque metro, East Mountains and Estancia valley); high = northern mountains (Sangre de Cristo, Jemez, Santa Fe, Taos, Chama, Raton) and a second box for the Sacramento Mountains (Ruidoso, Cloudcroft); west = Four Corners, Navajo/Zuni country, Grants/Gallup and Catron County; plains = the eastern plains (Clovis, Tucumcari, Clayton, Hobbs). Everything else (Chihuahuan desert: Las Cruces, Alamogordo, Roswell, Carlsbad, Deming, Silver City) is desert.
_rename: Use the form people actually say: 'Eldorado at Santa Fe' CDP is known as Eldorado; 'Pueblo of Sandia Village' as Sandia Pueblo.
_cdp: CDPs are kept when pop2010 >= cdpMinPop, not excluded, without a hyphen and without a drop word; keepCdp overrides all of that.
_excludeCdp: Military CDPs (AFB, White Sands Missile Range housing), an agribusiness HQ (Napi Headquarters), subdivision-style names (Acres, Knolls, Meadows, Farm, Park), generic words and names of bigger places elsewhere (San Jose, Monterey Park, University Park).
_keepCdp: Well-known places below the floor or hidden by the drop-word/hyphen filter (South Valley, North Valley, Yah-ta-hey, Upper Fruitland), Amtrak's Lamy, Turquoise Trail and high-road villages, and 2020 CDPs with no 2010 count (Ojo Caliente, Isleta, Fruitland, Gamerco, Tortugas).
_setSide: Turquoise Trail villages (Santa Fe County) fall in the gap between the rio and high polygons.
